Marissa — putting together the export now. Summary / notes: 

- Retention & residency: FinCo’s dedicated deployment is configured for 13 months retention; logs are stored encrypted at rest in the US region and keys are customer-specific KMS keys.
- Export format: CSV (UTF-8), gzip-compressed for transfer. Attached: fincobank_audit_logs_export_2026-04-13.csv (sample subset) and access_report_readme.txt. README includes column definitions.
- Columns included: timestamp_utc, actor_id, actor_type, identity_email, endpoint, action, resource_id, request_id, payload_contains_pii (true/false), response_status, bytes_transferred.
- PII in payloads: Our runtime does not persist raw request payloads by default. However, for customers who opt into detailed debugging or data capture (explicitly enabled by customer), raw request content may be present. For FinCo’s tenant we do NOT have global raw payload capture enabled. The payload_contains_pii flag is derived from an automated tokenizer-based detector run at ingestion — it is conservative and flags possible PII to help scope reviews.
- Redaction: For exports where raw payloads are present, we provide a redacted export and note the redaction policy in the README. Since FinCo does not have raw payload capture enabled, the export will not contain request bodies.
- Access controls & proof: Audit logs include a separate column "actor_role" reflecting internal user/service role; we can also provide IAM change events if auditors need proof of who had access.
- Timing: I’ve generated a full export for 2025-10-01 -> 2026-03-31; delivery method options: secure S3 access (pre-signed URL) or encrypted email (PGP). Recommend pre-signed URL to their security bucket.

Attaching sample files now. If legal review is required for delivery, flag and I’ll loop in legal.

Ben Carter
Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
